**Background.** Obesity affects more than one billion adults globally, constituting one of the most consequential public health crises of the twenty-first century and a leading driver of preventable morbidity and premature mortality [@NCDRiskFactor2016Trends; @GBD20152017Health].

**Methods.** We conducted a PRISMA-compliant systematic review of randomised controlled trials, meta-analyses, and clinical practice guidelines published between January 2016 and December 2024. PubMed, Scopus, and Embase were searched using pre-specified MeSH and free-text terms encompassing lifestyle intervention, anti-obesity pharmacotherapy, and bariatric surgery. Eligibility was restricted to publications appearing in Q1 or Q2 journals as defined by CiteScore quartile ranking (minimum CiteScore 3.0). Fifty-four primary studies met inclusion criteria after independent dual screening and PRISMA-guided exclusion.

**Results.** Subcutaneous semaglutide 2.4 mg once weekly (STEP 1 trial; n = 1,961) produced a mean body weight reduction of 14.9% versus 2.4% with placebo over 68 weeks (p < 0.001) [@Wilding2021Once]. The dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist tirzepatide demonstrated superior efficacy in SURMOUNT-1 (n = 2,539), with the 15 mg dose achieving a mean weight loss of 20.9% compared with 3.1% for placebo at 72 weeks (p < 0.001) [@Jastreboff2022Tirzepatide]. Beyond weight reduction, the SELECT cardiovascular outcomes trial (n = 17,604) established that semaglutide 2.4 mg reduces the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) by 20% in persons with established cardiovascular disease and obesity but without diabetes (hazard ratio 0.80; 95% CI 0.72–0.90; p < 0.001) [@Lincoff2023Semaglutide]. In the SURMOUNT-NASH trial, tirzepatide resolved metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) without worsening fibrosis in 62.4% of participants receiving 10 mg and 79.1% receiving 15 mg, compared with 9.7% in the placebo group [@Loomba2024Tirzepatide]. Bariatric surgery continues to offer the greatest magnitude and durability of weight loss, with the Swedish Obese Subjects study demonstrating 60–80% excess weight loss maintained over ten years, while the STAMPEDE trial reported HbA1c below 6.0% without antidiabetic medication at five years in 29% of Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and 23% of sleeve gastrectomy recipients, versus 5% with intensive medical therapy alone [@Schauer2017Bariatric; @Sjoström2004Lifestyle].

**Conclusions.** The period 2016–2024 has been transformative for obesity medicine. Novel GLP-1 receptor agonists and dual GIP/GLP-1 agonists now achieve 15–21% body weight reductions unprecedented for pharmacological agents, with semaglutide further demonstrating proven cardiovascular benefit. Precision approaches targeting individual metabolic phenotype and comorbidity burden are emerging as the field moves toward treating obesity as the chronic, relapsing disease that it is.
